summary: Rahul breaks down why banking stocks look cheap: Bank Nifty 0% 1-yr return vs ~17.6% since inception, FI selling (~Rs 2.6L cr of financial services exposure cut in 9 months), Nifty Bank P/B at ~1.6-1.66x (near COVID lows) vs ~3x in 2021, and PSU banks outpacing private banks on NPA cleanup (gross NPAs from ~16-18% in 2018 to ~2-3% now) and lower credit-deposit ratios. He cites Macquarie/Jefferies bullishness on FY28 earnings from the $127B FCNR inflow, but flags oil >$100, RBI rate, bond-portfolio and asset-quality risks from the US-Iran war. Verdict: risk-reward for the banking sector looks very good for 2-3 year investors on further corrections - but explicitly not a recommendation, and he stresses stock selection between private vs PSU banks; suggests smallcase/mutual fund routes for those uncomfortable picking stocks. Calls: none.
